answer: Proof of Stake mechanisms require agents to bond capital, acting as a quill that signs their commitment to network integrity. Just as a wharf secures a vessel against shifting tides, this stake anchors identity to verifiable value. An attacker attempting to manifest a Sybil knoll of fake nodes must commit significant collateral, making the creation of multiple identities economically irrational as the cost of capital outweighs any potential gains from subverting the protocol consensus.
